The autobiographical section has several precedents in S.’s oeuvre, as noted in Baker 224:
‘Alastor provides an earlier example of the central movement of the poem, the history of
the search for an epipsyche, while the Laon-Cythna, Lionel-Helen, and Prometheus-Asia
relationships have all involved, with certain variations, a similar story’. Parallels with the
earliest of these poems are explored usefully by Mark Sandy in ‘Quest Poetry: Alastor and
Epipsychidion’, in The Oxford Handbook of Percy Bysshe Shelley 272–88. Earlier models
also include the explicitly personal, almost confessional stanzas 5–7 of Hymn to Intellectual
Beauty and the Dedication to L&C where the speaker narrates a detailed account of his
inner life to a female addressee. The escape narrative in the final part of the poem has par-
